m: 1. लट् (cf. √ रट्) cl. 1. P. लटति, ‘to be a child’ or ‘to cry’, Dhātup. ix, 11.
2. लट् (in gram.) a technical term for the terminations of the Present or for that tense itself (cf. 1. ल).
a: लट् — {c1c} P. (लटति) 1 To be a child. --2 To act like a child. --3 To talk like a child, prattle. --4 To cry.
लट् — A technical term used by Pāṇini to denote the Present tense or its terminations.

m: लटभा f. a handsome girl, beautiful woman, ib.
लटभ mfn. (cf. next and लडह) handsome, pretty, lovely, Vcar.
a: लटभ — a. (Connected with the Prākṛta लडह which appears to be derived from it) Charming, handsome, beautiful, attractive, lovely; अतिक्रांतः कालो लटभललनाभोगसुलभः Bh. 3. 32 (where commentators render लटभ by सलावण्य); तस्याः पादनखश्रेणिः शोभते लटभभुवः Vikr. 8. 6. Bilhaṇa has used this word in three more places of the same book, where it appears to mean ‘a young pretty woman’, ‘a handsome woman’; e. g. किं वा वर्णनया समस्तलटभालंकारतामेष्यति 8. 86; अनर्घ्यलावण्यनिधानभूमिर्न कस्य लोभं लटभा तनोति 9. 68; केशबंधविभबैर्लटभानां पिंडतामिव जगाम तमिस्रं 11. 18.
